findings.reason: Two occurrences of an inscription are distinct occurrences. Removing that distinction would remove the event across which the copula identifies them.
The act now recognising differs from the finished self-image it can recognise. Their identity-through-difference is the argument, not a machine-capacity caveat.

The two-person/same-name and changed-name/same-person examples distinguish reference from the sound carrying it. This prevents the naming/counting claim from becoming a claim that a word individuates by itself.
The equality of numerical value does not identify the physical inscriptions. The explicit respect makes the example exact.
Proposed-relative-to-circumstance means criterion-governed identification. It would be stronger and false to let the word proposed mean unconstrained choice.
A bare formula and its situated use carry different information. Speaker, intended possibility and respect of comparison are the positive constituents at issue.
The fourth is contextual holding of three persons, not a fourth person; 3:3/3:1 and 4:2 count different offices. This protects the actual personed derivation.

An exact third-person model and the first-person presence it concerns remain different offices in the interpersonal encounter. The statement asserts that relation positively; it is not an open-phenomenality disclaimer.
Agreement and opposition require a shared register. The immutable gap leaves identification possible across a non-coincidence; it is not a denial of identity.
Predication supplies a determinate presentation and identification maintains the bearer. The paired conditions distinguish those operations.
A repeated name cannot on its own distinguish two bearers. The source is the protected authorial Kripke encounter, not a newly verified Kripke theorem.
An account with no route for consequences to revise its terms prevents the return being argued. This is the defined failure of Count-to-Account.
Memory, permission and material arrangement constitute possible action. Treating them as scenery would contradict the explicit intervention examples.
A selected context frame differs from the region that can affect it. The finite frame is usable without being exhaustive.
A rule orders an expanse; an account of that rule differs from the expanse. Country Path and calque collation remain separate historical tasks, not a reason to suppress this philosophical relation.
The counted participant is distinguished through occurrence and circumstance, rather than automatically multiplied by descriptions or individuated by repeated sound.
Constitutional priority of discrimination gives naming its referent. No historical chronology of the invention of numbers and names is asserted.
Place-marker, operand and boundary expression admit different operations. The sign alone does not confer every arithmetic permission.
Arithmetic admission and psychic investigation concern distinct histories and objects. A represented item cannot take over the determining capacity whose representation it is.
Configuration and trajectory disclose different information. Neither is an adequate substitute for the other where history changes the available transitions.
Adding the saying to the count produces a further act of counting. The return recognises that activity instead of treating a final numeral as its enclosure.
A world-account remains an act within Life/Mind; an increase of represented detail does not invert the order of dependence.
A numeral alone does not contain the dataset, evaluator, comparison class and permission through which it governs an act. These distinct causes must remain reachable by a correction.
Identity is equal to difference in articulation and unequal in its identifying office. OR/AND preserves the different respects of the copula rather than asserting an unqualified contradiction.
The two are the operations composing the four appearances, not two unrelated extra objects. This is the actual 4+2 derivation.

Early File One loads 1 as a mark; core theorem IX loads it as integrated recognition. X also changes office between X/x and the object-field. Removing those distinctions would silently conflate actual source developments.
